_README.purpose: CANONICAL owner-decoded potion mechanics/timing, mirror of enemy_notes.json (created 2026-08-12 when the Stable Serum decode arrived; grep here before modeling potions or filing potion questions). The potion pass (PLAN 'THE POTION PASS') grows this into the full per-potion class/timing catalog.
_README.conventions: mechanic = owner decode (near-verbatim, dated). timing = when to drink/throw. traps = interactions that nullify or invert the value.

Stable Serum.timing: Hard to use. Owner suggestion: drink on elites or bosses at the END of a turn where the remaining unplayed cards are high quality -- the value is carrying a premium leftover hand into the next turns, so a round-1 'buff lane' drink is exactly wrong.
Stable Serum.traps: Holding Runic Pyramid ('you no longer discard your hand at the end of turn') its combat value is ZERO -- but owner clarification 2026-08-12: 'useless' means DISCARD IT IN FAVOR OF ANY OTHER POTION when slots contend, NOT drink/toss on the spot. An occupied slot still beats an empty one (events can pay/consume potions). So under Pyramid: keep-rank = strictly last, displaced by anything; never proactively dumped. Same interaction family as Restlessness x Pyramid. CORNER CASE (owner 2026-08-12, 'pretty arcane, might as well write it down'): holding Runic Pyramid AND Petrified Toad ('at the start of combat, add a Potion-shaped Rock into your inventory'), the empty-slot calculus INVERTS -- discard the Serum from the last slot JUST BEFORE combat, because the Toad refills the freed slot with a Rock at fight start, and any Rock beats a Pyramid-dead Serum. The keep-it-for-events rule applies only when nothing refills the slot.
Stable Serum.bot_status: Not yet specially handled: the text-heuristic lanes likely class it as a generic buff (round<=1 drink = worst timing). Proper end-of-good-turn lane + Pyramid veto belong to the potion pass; recorded here so the pass inherits the decode.
